title: Run a School Fair Booth
learning_objectives: Budget for booth supplies and inventory
Plan a snack menu with energy-giving options
Make team decisions and handle customer interactions

events.description: Your team is running a booth at the school fair! You have $100 and 6 hours. First, what kind of booth? Each option has different costs and earning potential.

choices.label: Snack booth — fruit cups + lemonade ($60 supplies, high demand)
choices.effect: Food always sells! $60 invested, high earning potential. $40 left for other needs.

choices.label: Game booth — ring toss + prizes ($45 supplies, steady demand)
choices.effect: Games attract a crowd! $45 in supplies, $55 left. Prizes cost less than food.

choices.label: Games + small snacks ($80 supplies, highest potential)
choices.effect: Double the fun! More setup but more ways to earn. $20 left for emergencies.

events.description: Time to schedule 6 hours of shifts for your 5 team members. Everyone needs at least one break. Two people at the booth at all times. How do you organize it?

choices.label: Rotating pairs — everyone works 3 hours with breaks
choices.effect: Fair rotation! Everyone works the same amount and gets breaks.

choices.label: Match people to roles — cashier, server, promoter
choices.effect: Specialized roles! The outgoing person promotes, the organized one handles money.

choices.label: Flexible sign-up — people pick their preferred hours
choices.effect: People work when they're most available! Some flexibility needed for gaps.

events.description: Midway through the fair, you're running low on supplies. You've earned $75 so far. The supply store nearby has what you need for $25. But a teammate wants to use the $25 to buy prizes for a raffle.

choices.label: Restock supplies — keep earning
choices.effect: Smart reinvestment! You restock and earn another $50 by the end of the fair.

choices.label: Raffle — one big draw at the end
choices.effect: The raffle creates excitement! People buy tickets and it draws a crowd.

choices.label: Split — $15 restock, $10 raffle prizes
choices.effect: A balanced approach! Partial restock AND a smaller raffle. Both strategies in play!

events.description: A parent complains that the prices are too high. A younger kid is upset because they didn't win a prize. Two situations at once! How does your team handle it?

choices.label: You handle the parent, teammate helps the kid
choices.effect: Team delegation! You calmly explain pricing while your teammate gives the kid a participation sticker.

choices.label: Offer a small discount + a 'try again free' coupon
choices.effect: Customer service! The parent feels heard and the kid gets another chance. Both leave happy.

choices.label: Quick team huddle — decide together
choices.effect: 30-second team meeting! You agree on a response and everyone's on the same page.

events.description: Fair's over! Time to count earnings and split any profits. Your team earned $150 total, spent $100 on supplies. That's $50 profit for 5 people.

choices.label: Split equally — $10 each
choices.effect: Fair and simple! Everyone gets $10 for their hard work.

choices.label: Donate profits to a school cause
choices.effect: The team votes to donate! The school thanks you and everyone feels great about giving back.

choices.label: Save it for the next school event booth
choices.effect: Reinvesting! Next time you'll start with $50 and need less startup money.

recap_template: You ran a school fair booth from start to finish! You managed money, scheduled a team, served customers, and handled surprises. That's real-world leadership across all four life skills!
positive_framing_rules: Never say the booth was unsuccessful or poorly managed
Frame customer complaints as learning opportunities
